sophia: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak, we're seeing 95th pct latency regressions on decode-heavy chat flows. Not obvious in small e2e tests, but production traces spike.

dan: ugh. Any profiler dumps or flamegraphs? which workload reproduces it best?

sophia: Repro is easy with the long-chat test harness (seq_len ~1500, streaming enabled). Attaching the condensed perf sample from last night (copied lines):

```
# perf sample (decode path)
worker id: gpu-12
avg decode batch size: 6.2
median decode latency (ms/token): 12.4 -> up from 8.1 after kernel switch
kernel chosen: attention_fw_v3 (fallback path)
kv cache hit ratio: 0.78 -> down from 0.92
notes: mixed-phase batches observed (prefill+decode in same kernel run)
```

liam: interesting — mixed-phase batches. We've seen kernel selector prefer prefill-optimized kernels when batches contain any long-prefill requests, which slows decode streaming.

nina: that matches a pattern I saw: prefill tokens have long seqs causing selector to choose transformer_kernel_x that is fast for prefill but penalizes decode incremental loops.

dan: so root cause could be batch formation fanout: a single GPU batch aggregates prefill + decode requests because the token budget window doesn't enforce phase affinity.

sophia: yeah. Short-term mitigation: pin phase-aware queueing so prefill and decode don't coalesce into the same kernel invocation. Proposed quick change:

```yaml
scheduler:
  phase_affinity: true   # new: keep prefill/decode separate per batch
  decode_token_budget: 24
  prefill_token_budget: 256
  allow_mixed_phase_for_burst: false
```

liam: i like it. Also, small-change idea: when kernel selector computes scores, add +Inf penalty if batch contains decode and kernel is prefill-optimized. That forces fallback to decode-friendly kernel.

nina: watch KV cache retention too. When we separate queues we might increase KV churn because prefill primes caches earlier. I'd add a kv_priming_grace param to hold KV pages for ~2s after prefill to improve decode hit ratio.

infra-bot: deploy-check: build passed on canary, but integration tests for streaming latency are flaky (timeout 120s). Recommend manual canary run on staging gpu-pool-2.

dan: can someone run a controlled canary with the phase_affinity flag on staging and collect 99/95/50 pct for decode streams? Also capture kernel selection logs.

sophia: i'll run the canary now on staging (gpu-pool-2). test script: `./tools/run_long_chat_canary --pool gpu-pool-2 --iters 500`.

liam: when you run it, include the lightweight sampler that dumps batch composition every 30s. Something like:

```
[30s sample] batch_id=452; tokens: prefill=1024 (1 req) decode=48 (6 reqs); kernel=attention_fw_v3
[30s sample] batch_id=459; prefill=0 decode=36 (5 reqs); kernel=incremental_attn_v2
```

nina: if we see too many mixed batches even with phase_affinity, we should reduce decode_token_budget to 12 and enable microbatch-split for decode to keep latency SLOs.

sophia: results: canary started, will post summary in ~10m. early snapshot: 95th decode latency down ~18% vs baseline with kernel switch but KV hit ratio dipped slightly. Posting full dump when done.

dan: sweet. action items: (1) sophia run canary + post logs, (2) liam prototype kernel-selector penalty, (3) nina add kv_priming_grace opt and bench, (4) infra-bot run secondary canary automation. we'll reconvene after logs.

nina: FYI — chances are this will be a tunable rather than permanent rollback. we want the kernel change but with phase-aware batching heuristics.

sophia: agree. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary run completed on staging/gpu-pool-2; artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1767894321-phase-affinity-1.tar.gz
